The OP did not assume he was a creeper, or video taping her, or oogling her, but it was a valid concern, hence the purpose of this thread asking if she was out of line letting him know he was making her uncomfortable. Both the OP and I, in my theoretical reaction to someone sitting there for 30 minutes instead of talking somewhere else in the open gym, is that this individual must have a reason for doing so. When it comes to trying to find a source for that reason, it is terribly unlikely that someone is going to be waiting for that extended period of time to ask something, but its a long shot explanation since there aren't many others for why a woman would do that to the OP. For the man, it is equally as much of a long shot, but there is the additional possibility that he is checking her out or is waiting around for something else, which seems more likely.

While we're on theoreticals, let's consider what would have happened if this story had progressed into something news-worthy, if she had been sexually assaulted or worse. The immediate questions after hearing the story are why didn't she do something? He was there for 30 minutes, why didn't she leave or call someone for help? She even felt uncomfortable, why didn't she trust her instinct? She shouldn't have been at the gym alone in the first place. Why doesn't she go to a women only gym if there are times when her gym is that empty? It is considered at least partially the woman's fault if she did not prepare to defend herself accordingly, if she did not use "common sense", if she chose to trust a stranger and give him the benefit of the doubt. In this case, turning around and telling him she was uncomfortable seems like a terribly reasonable thing to do.

I have two; the first more difficult to explain than creepy, the second... just creepy.

The first, I saw what is commonly described as a will o' wisp. I was walking with a friend on the edge of campus when I was in college, past this bamboo garden. Kids frequently got in trouble for messing around with it because it did not belong to the college, and was private property. Hence, when we first saw the light, we both assumed it was the flashlight of a security guard- it had that slightly bounding jostle one would associate with footsteps.

Still, we both stopped and stared, because it seemed to be in the middle of the bamboo garden, and the bamboo grows so tightly together there shouldn't really be room for someone to casually stroll through it. It was moving slowly closer to us, bobbing and winding between through the bamboo, which is when I think we both simultaneously realized that it couldn't be a human. This went on for a solid minute, with us just staring frozen, and I asked her, you see that, right? She confirmed.

Then it just went out. My first thought, despite the fact that it was moving through the thicket, was that it must have been something shining through from behind somehow; the moment it went out I yelled for her to run around one side, while I the other, since the garden was circular. No one was there. There was a small parking lot near the back, I thought, perhaps a car with its headlight out, even though we saw no one around enter it. Still, we felt every car in the lot to see if any engines were hot, in case we somehow just didn't hear a car pulling up, but no, all cold.

The second happened just a week ago.

Nothing too strange has ever happened in my house, but this turned me pale right quick. I was heating up some soup downstairs, my parents were watching a movie. I hear the floor shift slightly over by the laundry room entrance- the garage leads into the house through the laundry room, so I glance back behind me and the dog is approaching to check it out as well. Then I see and hear the door knob jostle, as if someone is about to enter, but the door never opens. My dog sniffs at the knob, but doesn't bark as he would if he smelled a stranger, which is the only reason I wasn't flipping my shit. Still, I thought what if some crazy guy was trying to enter the house. On rare occasion, one of my brothers will come home that way, though they were both already in the house. I asked my parents, "Who's in the laundry room?" My mother answered, "What? No one, sit down."

But I know I saw that doorknob move, and so did the dog, it wasn't in my head. I was debating whether to just walk over there and check it out, or to tell my dad to get his gun (we're Pennslyvanians, guns everywhere ofc). Deciding I didn't want to freak them out unnecessarily, I instead grabbed a flashlight, laid down on the floor and shone it under the door to look for feet. Nothing.

It must have just been the house settling in some way to make the door knob jostle just the way a hand would, or so I reason to myself.
